I HATE shopping. I cannot stress this enough. I have two weddings to attend in October and I'm dreading shopping for an appropriate dress (different climates). I went to five weddings last year in the same dress, hopefully I can get away with doing the same this wedding season...

My wardrobe has suffered because of this, so I do try to buy fewer, sturdy, quality pieces to decrease the amount of future shopping I'll have to do.

Some tips I use to lesson my agony: Sale racks with nice stuff but weird sizes - buy larger items and have them tailored. It'll be worth it.

You're already looking at secondhand stores, so same rules apply. Larger items can be taken in.

Many of my friends have attended clothing swaps with some success, but I've found that the styles vary too much for my (unfortunately vanilla) style. Same idea applies about having the items tailored to fit you.

If you can't find any that are cheap, I would say buy three really stylish and quality skirts from whatever online retailer or shop you love but can never justify splurging on. I think it's better to spend a hundred bucks on something that will last for years that 20 on something that will wear out after 6 months, and it'll most likely look better.

TL;DR Buy weird or ill-fitting sizes off the sale rack and have them tailored, or splurge on some quality items that will last for years.
